feedback.worked_solution:
Since $∠AOD$ is a straight angle, the angles $∠AOE$ and $∠DOE$ are supplementary. Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to ${180}^{∘}.$ 

So, the measure of the angle $∠AOE$ that's supplementary to the angle of $∠DOE=5x-{5}^{∘}$ must be

$$
\begin{aligned}∠AOE & ={180}^{∘}-(5x-5)^{∘} \\  & =({180}^{∘}+{5}^{∘})-5{x}^{∘} \\  & ={(185-5x)}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the points $A,C,$ and $D$ lie on the circle. We know that the radius of the circle is $r=OC.$

We first notice that

$$
AD=AO+OD.
$$

Now, $\overset{―}{AO}$ and $\overset{―}{OD}$ are both segments between the center of the circle and the circle itself. So, they are both radii of the circle, and because $AD=8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =8 \\ AO+OD & =8 \\ r+r & =8 \\ 2r & =8 \\ r & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
OC=r=4.
$$
